recommended_disposition: reclassify as unresolved/mitigation-proposed-never-adopted; do not enter dataset as a failure-and-recovery episode
headline: The metric that defines the failure (DRC count), the stage named as failed (GRT), and the knobs turned (GRT-only parameters) are three different things; the record's own gaps array destroys the causal claim while confidence 0.8 asserts one.

confidence_assessment.reason: The record asserts a recovery it does not measure, from a change it does not show was adopted, against a metric its stated knobs cannot move.

findings.claim: '20k routing congestion DRCs' reported as a GRT failure, addressed by GRT-only knobs.
findings.why_wrong: DRC violations are not a GRT output. Global routing reports congestion/overflow (total overflow, worst overflow, congested-GCell count); DRCs come from detailed_route/check_drc. The two knobs in the intervention (routing-layer adjustment, -congestion_iterations) are GRT-only and cannot move a DRC count produced downstream. Either prior_state is wrong (it was a detail-route/DRC failure, not a GRT failure) or observation is wrong (20k was overflow/GCells, not DRCs). As written the intervention targets a different metric than the one that defines the incident.
findings.correction: Name one stage: global_route. Replace 'DRC' with the GRT metric verbatim from the log (total overflow / worst overflow / congested-GCell count). If 20k really is DRC, then the stage is detailed_route and the two GRT knobs are irrelevant to it.

findings.why_wrong: A GRT run completing is not evidence that congestion went away: GRT completes by default and prints overflow on the way out. gaps admits no re-measured count and no runtime. The gaps field and the confidence field contradict each other directly.
findings.correction: Either report post-change total/worst overflow and congested-GCell count, or set intervention_caused_recovery confidence <=0.2 and label post_state as 'run completed; effect unmeasured'.

findings.why_wrong: The issue was closed not_planned with no PR, and gaps concedes merge status is unknown. A maintainer's in-thread suggestion that the project declined is a proposed_intervention, not a chosen_intervention. The field name launders a rejected suggestion into an adopted fix.
findings.correction: Rename to intervention_proposed; add intervention_status = 'proposed in-thread 2024-11-14; no PR; closed not_planned (Stale); not adopted upstream'.

findings.claim: Low density plus localized congestion presented as a paradox; macro-looping hypothesis listed as a separate, deferred side issue.
findings.why_wrong: prior_state says open space at the top of the die; observation says the hot region is at the top of the die and around the macro. That is not a paradox, it is one fact: a hot corridor inside empty area is the signature of a detour around the macro. The heatmap is confirmatory evidence FOR the #5971 hypothesis, yet the intervention (a global capacity knob) does not address it and the record never draws this line.
findings.correction: Promote macro-detour to hypothesis_primary, cite the heatmap's location-in-empty-area as the supporting evidence, and state explicitly that the layer-adjustment change treats the symptom (modeled capacity) rather than the cause (wiring demand from the detour).

findings.claim: Layer adjustment 0.45 -> 0.2 framed as a fix.
findings.why_wrong: set_global_routing_layer_adjustment blocks a fraction of a layer's tracks from GRT: 0.45 blocks 45% (55% usable), 0.2 blocks 20% (80% usable). The change increases modeled capacity by roughly 45% rather than improving routing; GRT 'completing' is close to tautological, and the displaced cost would surface at detail route, which was never run. gaps calls the missing semantics a documentation nit, but the entire causal claim is unintelligible without them.
findings.correction: State the mechanism in the episode (0.45 -> 0.2 = usable tracks 55% -> 80%, a capacity-model relaxation), and mark the result as unvalidated until detail route + check_drc are measured.

findings.claim: Two knobs moved; attribution to the pair.
findings.why_wrong: Layer adjustment 0.45->0.2 and iterations 30->35 were applied together. candidates_considered says iterations were 'asked early on and swept' but reports no sweep outcome, so there is no basis to attribute convergence to either change or to rule out that layer adjustment alone did it.
findings.correction: Report the 2x2 sweep as a table, or state attribution is impossible and confidence in the intervention must reflect that.

findings.claim: 'the default 30 congestion iterations were also insufficient'; 'changed ... to 35'.
findings.why_wrong: 'default 30' is asserted twice in the record but is a single unsourced claim. If the actual default exceeds 35, then 'changed to 35' is a decrease and the 'default was insufficient so we raised it' narrative inverts completely.
findings.correction: Verify the default for this ORFS build and state it as sourced; if default > 35, rewrite the iteration half of the hypothesis.

findings.claim: 'the routing layer adjustments from 0.45 to 0.2' as bare scalars.
findings.why_wrong: set_global_routing_layer_adjustment takes a per-layer argument and asap7/ORFS applies non-uniform adjustments across the stack. Bare scalars are unreproducible; uniformly relaxing every layer is a materially different and more dangerous act than relaxing the few layers the congested corridor uses.
findings.correction: Name the affected layers and their before/after values; note whether the change was uniform or targeted.

findings.claim: '20k ... DRCs at only 0.24 placement density' as the headline anomaly.
findings.why_wrong: 0.24 is a global average while the congestion is explicitly localized. Low global density plus a hard macro plus concentrated local congestion is expected, not anomalous. The framing manufactures a mystery instead of reporting the real one (why the detour exists, i.e. #5971).
findings.correction: Retitle as 'localized congestion in a macro-adjacent detour corridor despite 0.24 global density' and drop the implied paradox.

findings.why_wrong: not_planned is a close state, Stale is a label; 'Stale' is not a GitHub close reason. Also the quote is dated 2024-11-14 while closure is 2026 - a ~14-month gap before a stale bot fires is implausible, so the quote date, the closure year, or 'automatically' is wrong.
findings.correction: Separate close state from label; reconcile the timeline against the thread.

findings.why_wrong: Second-person/author voice leaked into a dataset field; the episode is written from the issue author's perspective rather than the curator's.
Hyphenated form is a docs-anchor slug; the Tcl command is set_global_routing_layer_adjustment.
findings.correction: Use the underscored command name; keep the docs anchor separately as a URL.

findings.why_wrong: That is a reproduction command, not an observation; and it yields a GUI session, not a reported number.
findings.correction: Move to a reproduction field; state the actual artifact (GRT log / congestion report / heatmap export) that carries the 20k figure.

findings.why_wrong: #5971 was deferred and never attempted here; listing it as a considered candidate implies evaluation and rejection.

findings.claim: Quote truncated with ellipsis; post_state reads it as full confirmation; 'complete BoomTile' vs 'complete GRT'.
findings.why_wrong: The quote is cut mid-sentence so the reader cannot see whether a caveat follows; and 'complete BoomTile' (whole flow) is silently downgraded to 'complete GRT' (one stage) in post_state, which is the weaker and more defensible claim.
findings.correction: Quote the full sentence; preserve the flow-vs-stage distinction rather than collapsing it.

findings.why_wrong: No seed, no global_route invocation, no congestion report artifact, no preserved heatmap, no runtime.
findings.correction: Attach the GRT log lines, the congestion report, and the heatmap image; record the seed and the exact ORFS script invocation.

findings.claim: Any retained DRC count on asap7.
findings.why_wrong: asap7 is a predictive PDK, so any DRC count is measured against an approximate deck rather than a production signoff deck.
findings.correction: Footnote that retained DRC figures are against the predictive asap7 deck.

corrected_version.title: BoomTile (asap7, ORFS): GRT overflow concentrated in a macro-adjacent detour corridor despite 0.24 global placement density; mitigated only by relaxing the GRT capacity model - macro root cause deferred (#5971), change never adopted
corrected_version.metric: GRT congestion: total overflow, worst overflow, congested-GCell count. NOT DRC - DRC is a detailed_route/check_drc artifact and is not produced by GRT.
corrected_version.prior_state: BoomTile (MegaBoom-derived) in asap7, ORFS v3.0-1735-gdefc349e. Standard-cell placement density 0.24, with open area concentrated at the top of the die. global_route did not reach acceptable overflow.
corrected_version.observation: 20k <congested GCells | total-overflow units - RECORD MUST NAME THE METRIC> reported by GRT. The congestion heatmap is contiguous with the macro halo and extends into the empty top-of-die region. That spatial pattern is consistent with a detour corridor around the macro rather than with a global capacity shortage.
corrected_version.hypothesis_primary: Nets loop around the macro and funnel through the open top-of-die region (#5971). Supported by the heatmap: the hot region lies in empty area, which is what a detour looks like.
corrected_version.hypothesis_secondary: Modeled per-layer capacity is over-conservative for this design (layer adjustment 0.45 = 45% of tracks blocked).
corrected_version.candidates_considered: 2x2 sweep required, results currently unreported: {layer_adj 0.45, 0.2} x {congestion_iterations DEFAULT, 35}. As reported both changes were applied together, so attribution is impossible.
corrected_version.intervention_proposed: Reduce set_global_routing_layer_adjustment on layers {UNSPECIFIED - MUST BE NAMED} from 0.45 to 0.2 (55% -> 80% usable tracks, i.e. a capacity-model relaxation rather than a routing improvement); raise -congestion_iterations to 35.
corrected_version.intervention_status: Proposed in-thread by eder-matheus (MEMBER), 2024-11-14. No PR. Issue closed not_planned (Stale label), i.e. NOT adopted upstream.
corrected_version.post_state: GRT reported to complete in a local run. No overflow re-measurement, no detail-route or check_drc validation, no runtime. Because the change relaxes the capacity model, 'GRT completes' is a weak result: the displaced cost would appear at detail route, which was never measured.
corrected_version.why_mitigation_not_fix: The knob increases modeled track supply rather than reducing wiring demand; the named root cause (macro looping, #5971) was explicitly deferred and remains open.

required_experiments_before_acceptance.design: Run baseline (layer_adj 0.45, default iterations), then 0.2/default, then 0.45/35, then 0.2/35.
required_experiments_before_acceptance.then: Take the winning corner through detailed_route + check_drc and report DRC count and runtime.
required_experiments_before_acceptance.acceptance_rule: Do not admit as a recovery episode until a corner clears detail route without regressing DRCs. Until then it is a report of a number going down because the ruler got longer.
